correctness.rationale: The proof partitions the leading three-by-three Hankel block into invertible, singular with nonzero top-left second minor, singular rank-two with zero second minor in two explicit normal-form cases, and rank at most one. In each case the bordered determinant identity determines exact target-fiber counts. The quadratic character convolution is valid for every odd finite field, while the Frobenius map treats even characteristic separately. All expressions work at t=0. The five-field exhaustive direct determinant verifier (including GF(4)) corroborates the formula, but the infinite family is proved symbolically; no finite experiment is used as an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: García-Armas–Ghorpade–Ram Theorem 5.1 counts by rank and Dwivedi–Grinberg Theorem 1.5 fixes prefixes but still counts bounded rank/zero determinant. Neither theorem logically determines the distinct positive prescribed-determinant fibers exhibited here (e.g. \(q=5\) yields 16500 at 1 and 15000 at 2). The classical Daykin work is cited as rank-count antecedent, not falsely excluded by snippets; its original full text was inaccessible, giving the stated bibliographic risk. Targeted published-record searches under determinant, Hankel, Toeplitz, persymmetric, and catalecticant aliases did not identify this 4-by-4 formula; absence of a hit is not a novelty proof.
residual_risks: Original Daykin (1960) full text could not be inspected; a nonzero-determinant or bordered-variable variant may already imply this theorem despite citations suggesting the rank theorem only.
Potential older binary-sextic catalecticant or persymmetric terminology could conceal an equivalent fixed-value distribution.

value.rationale: The determinant-value distribution is a natural complete invariant of a random structured matrix ensemble, sharper than the classical rank/singularity distribution. It distinguishes quadratic residues and, when \(q\equiv1\pmod4\), fourth-power classes; in contrast characteristic two yields genuinely uniform fibers. The 4-by-4 case is the first displayed stratum with separate square and fourth-power root multiplicities; the exact full-fiber count is motivated by structured-matrix determinants and Toeplitz/catalecticant interpretations, not by an arbitrary subfamily or a numerically isolated gain.
